title: Adaptive Canary Signal Pruning & LTS Compatibility Validator
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Ship a stability controller that reduces false-positive canary failures and verifies LTS-channel compatibility before progressive rollouts. The controller will ingest smoke, perf, and eval signals and apply adaptive pruning and weighted aggregation so transient noise (e.g., garbage collector jitter, ephemeral network blips, short-lived cache cold starts) does not trigger aborts for LTS releases.

Scope:
- New "stability controller" service component in release-orchestrator that computes a single pass/fail score per canary population.
- Heuristic pruning algorithm: burst detection + rolling median smoothing + minimum sample retention window to avoid reacting to <10s spikes.
- Weighted gate: combine smoke-test binary, perf delta (p95 latency / token cost), and eval accuracy regressions into a normalized risk score.
- TTL-based signal suppression for known noisy probes (synthetic KV-cache warmers, long-gen stressers).
- Integrations: rollout engine (for automatic rollback), Console dashboard (visualize raw signals and pruned traces), CI job templates (jenkins/github actions) for preflight runs, and canary traffic split automation.
- Metrics & alerts: new telemetry for pruned_signal_ratio, stability_score, time_to_recover_after-spike, false_positive_rate (post-release).

Design constraints & trade-offs:
- Strong preference for simple heuristics over heavy ML models to keep predictable debugability.
- Must operate on streaming telemetry with bounded memory; retention limited to 30m rolling windows.
- Controller must be feature-flagged per-project and default off for non-LTS channels.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
1) Controller runs in the release pipeline and produces stability_score for canaries within 60s after canary start.
2) False-positive rate measured on the last 3 internal rollouts decreases by >=40% compared to baseline.
3) Rollout engine honors controller pass/fail decisions and triggers automated rollback for LTS rollouts when score > threshold.
4) Console shows pruned traces and raw signals with ability to toggle pruning on/off for investigations.
5) Playbook and runbook updated; on-call knows rollback run steps and how to inspect pruned traces.

Out of scope: full ML-based anomaly detection, offline historical batch re-scoring, changing probe definitions across teams (will be follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Controller computes stability_score within 60s of canary start
Measured false-positive rate for internal LTS rollouts reduced by >=40% vs baseline
Rollout engine takes controller decision to automatically rollback when score breaches threshold
Console shows both pruned and raw telemetry with toggle to disable pruning for investigations
Runbook/playbook updated and on-call trained on new signals
